summary: A refused prompt becomes a reported failure with the pattern name, instead of an unhandled rejection nobody sees

coordination.notes: The gate still throws - a leak must stop the call rather than produce a value somebody might log - and a distinct PrivacyGateError type is what lets the worker convert it without swallowing genuine bugs alongside it. Catching Error would relabel a typo in a provider as a privacy refusal, so there is a check for exactly that. One helper serves both call sites rather than two copies of the same catch. The refusal carries pattern names only; a test asserts the value never appears in the outcome or in the job note, since a diagnostic quoting the secret would be the leak the gate exists to prevent. Unreachable through the shipped request shape today, which is the argument usually used for leaving such a hole; it is fixed anyway, and the test reaches it through the caller-supplied instructions.
